title: Docara Project DNA
summary: A content-first, deterministic and portable static-site generator built from Markdown, declarative composition and SIMAI Framework Smart components.
purpose: Let an author build documentation, knowledge bases and landing pages from understandable files without coupling editorial content to the rendering engine.
principles: One public route in one locale has exactly one content/<locale>/<route>.md source file.
content/<locale>/lang.json is the only source of shared public UI strings; public resources/i18n and site.json compatibility do not exist.
Content, composition, presentation and engine logic have separate owners.
Markdown is compiled into immutable typed Document IR in memory before rendering; serialization is optional disposable evidence or cache.
Every node is rendered through one registry and every Smart component through one gateway.
Full and single-page builds use the same PageBuilder.
Generated artifacts are disposable and never become editorial sources.
SIMAI Framework owns tokens, utilities and universal UI; Docara composes them.
Diagnostics point back to the source Markdown location.
Unpublished legacy compatibility is removed instead of preserved.
non_goals: Store public documentation prose in PHP arrays, language packs, resources/i18n or site.json.
Maintain Jigsaw, Mix, trustedMainHtml or parallel projector pipelines.
Claim production or release readiness before independent acceptance.
quality_bar: A new contributor can find the source of a page, component and layout without chat history.
Two clean builds from the same immutable inputs are byte-identical.
One-page build and full build produce semantically identical output for the same route.
Unknown syntax and parameters fail with file, line and column diagnostics.
No public page is generated from a hidden catalog or language-pack record.
success_definition: A clean starter can author, build, inspect, update and reproduce a multilingual Docara site through one documented pipeline, while the repository contains no active parallel content or rendering architecture.
